items.title: How much does detection speed actually change the damage?
items.description: Northlake's real numbers: an ~332-record-per-night exfiltration rate, undetected for 11 nights, added up to the ~3,650 records the post-mortem reports. Dwell time is a direct multiplier on total exposure — drag how many days pass before containment against how many records leak per day to see how much a faster page, or a slower one, would have changed the outcome.

items.title: How much of the 72-hour disclosure window is actually left?
items.description: GDPR's clock starts at confirmed awareness, not at when the breach began — Northlake's team had it start at Day 11, 09:00, and filed at Day 13, 06:40, using most of the window on confirming scope and drafting an accurate notification. Drag hours elapsed since awareness to see how the remaining window shrinks, and where it hits zero.
